title: Agent policy
description: The L1 operator policy (agent-policy.yaml): autonomy tier per machine profile, what is never read, never done, asked about, or pre-approved, network egress, and run ceilings. Engine-neutral; compiled per engine by the adapters (adapters/*/README.md). Walls are denies (forbid, deny_read); ask is a human checkpoint and protects nothing unattended (ADR-0021).

profiles.description: Machine profile name (the dotfiles' .profile) -> its autonomy tier.

deny_read.description: Path globs no agent may read (secrets, credentials). A wall: compiled to a deny on every engine or the compile fails.

forbid.description: Walls: actions denied in every mode, on every profile.

ask.description: Human checkpoints: prompt a person at a terminal. Unattended they are denials; never count them as protection.

allow.description: Pre-approvals: run without asking. Never loosens a forbid or deny_read (deny wins on every engine).

roles.description: Who runs headless, and what each run may do (1.4.0): role name (author, evaluator, reader, planner, merge, ...) -> an overlay that only narrows the profile. When a policy names roles, every unattended run is one of them: an unattended compile emits one file set per role that runs on the engine (roles/<role>/), and an unattended profile's engine that no role names is a compile error. Interactive and bypass tiers have no allowlist boundary and ignore roles.

hooks.description: Hooks the compile emits for the user scope (1.4.0). forbid_guard: the engine-neutral guard (tools/guards/forbid-guard.mjs) that denies a shell command any command forbid matches however it is spelled (compound, wrapped, sh -c), registered as a PreToolUse hook on engines that share that hook protocol. Defense in depth: the project's own hook deny stays the wall.

requires_config.description: What the requires probes check (1.4.0; harness check-requires, harness run). prod_hosts: production endpoints (host or host:port, 443 by default) that a TCP connect from this host must fail to reach for prod-unreachable-from-this-host to pass; list addresses to probe the route rather than the resolver.

budgets.description: Run ceilings by tier. An unattended tier must have one.

accept_gaps.description: Degradations the operator accepts on purpose: an engine that cannot represent a field. Without an entry the compiler fails closed.

profiles.description: The profiles the acceptance covers (1.4.0). Without it, every profile except a bypass-tier (autonomous) one: a bypass profile's gaps are accepted only by an entry that names it, since its isolation is specific to that machine (HAR-4).

allOf.description: Some profile is unattended -> budgets.unattended is required (an unattended run has a ceiling).

tier.description: How often an agent asks. read-only: never writes. ask: asks before edits and commands. auto-edit: edits in the workspace without asking, asks for commands. auto: does not ask for routine actions; the engine's classifier reviews each action and blocks or asks for risky ones, ask rules still prompt, walls hold; an engine with no classifier mode compiles it to its stricter auto-edit equivalent (adapters). autonomous: does not ask, walls hold (interactive operator present). unattended: headless, never asks, asks become denials, the allowlist is the boundary.

engines.description: Engines installed on this profile; the compiler emits only these.

sandbox.description: This profile's sandbox, merged key by key over the top-level sandbox (a key set here replaces the top-level one; lists are replaced, not joined).

egress.description: This profile's egress, merged key by key over the top-level egress; the result needs a default, and a deny default an allow list.

requires.description: Named preconditions the operator keeps outside the policy for this profile to be safe, each a probe harness check-requires runs on the host: prod-unreachable-from-this-host (requires_config.prod_hosts), non-root, container, non-root-container, sandbox-available; an unknown name fails closed. Mandatory for the bypass tier (autonomous): the compiler refuses that tier without it, and harness run refuses to start the profile's runs until every probe passes (HAR-4).

engines.description: The engines that run this role (default: every engine the profile installs).

read_only.description: The role writes nothing: every write allow is dropped and every write denied (Claude Edit(**), Codex the :read-only sandbox, Gemini its write tools).

allow.description: The role's pre-approvals, replacing the profile's; each must be one the profile's allow already grants (role-narrows).

egress.description: The role's egress: deny by default, with these domains allowed; each must be one the profile's egress already allows (role-narrows).

fail_if_unavailable.description: Refuse to run rather than run unsandboxed.

writable_roots.description: Directories beyond the workspace that sandboxed commands may write.

credentials.description: Credentials sandboxed commands may use without reading them: each file or environment variable is masked (commands see a placeholder; the sandbox proxy restores the real value only on requests to inject_hosts, or to every allowed domain when it names none). A mask is not a wall: it does not cover the agent's own file tools, and a path deny_read names cannot also be masked.

path.description: One credential file, home-relative or absolute (no glob, no directory: a mask covers a single file).

env.description: An environment variable holding a credential.

extract.description: With path: a regex whose first group is the secret within the file, so tools still parse the rest.

inject_hosts.description: Hosts the real value may reach (plain host names); each must also be in the egress allow list.

pathGlob.description: A path glob: relative to each workspace root (**/.env), home-relative (~/.ssh/**) or absolute (//etc/** is not used; write /etc/**).

domain.description: A host, *.host for subdomains only, or **.host for the apex and subdomains.

argvToken.description: One literal argv token, or alternatives at that position.

rule.description: Exactly one matcher: command (an argv prefix, matched token by token), write (a path glob for file writes and edits), or tool (an abstract tool).

flags_anywhere.description: With command, in forbid only (1.4.0): the rule matches when the command words appear in that order anywhere in the argv (options, wrappers and a program path between or before them allowed: git -C . push, env git push) and any token after the last word is one of these flags. A flag matches a token exactly; one ending in * matches every token it begins (+* is a forced refspec). Combined short flags (-uf) are tokens of their own: list them.

domain.description: With tool: web-fetch only, the domain the rule covers.

examples.description: Commands the rule must match; compiled to Codex match = [...] and checked by tests.
